units.text: EXT. WELL-DIGGING CAMP - DESERT - DAY
A dry plain under a white sky.
A scaffold of timbers stands over a deep shaft.
A windlass creaks.
A water barrel stands empty in the shade of a tilting wagon.
EZRA LOCKRIDGE, 50s, sunburnt, sleeves rolled, hauls a bucket of rock and clay up from the shaft hand over hand.
MERCY TAVARES, 30s, in a broad straw hat, stands at the lip of the pit and holds the rope steady.
She is thin, tireless, and has not spoken for a long time.
The bucket clears the rim.
Ezra tips it.
A thin trickle of mud slides out.
He kneels, takes a pinch, and rubs it between his fingers.
Wet.
units.name: EZRA

units.text: Wet isn't water.
units.name: MERCY

units.text: It's near.
units.name: EZRA

units.text: You said that yesterday.
units.name: MERCY

units.text: He wipes his hands on his trousers.
He rises, stiff.
The wind carries a dull sound from the east, the clop of a single horse.
They turn.
A rider approaches along the dry riverbed, slowly, a long shadow thrown ahead of him.
He is tall and spare, with a black coat and a silver star on his lapel.
ANSEL WHITCOMBE, 40s, a land agent, reins in at the edge of camp and dismounts.
Morning.
units.name: ANSEL

units.text: It's near noon.
units.name: EZRA

units.text: So it is. I'm told you've been digging on the Culver claim.
units.name: ANSEL

units.text: I'm told it's nobody's claim.
units.name: EZRA

units.text: It's the bank's, as of Tuesday.
units.name: ANSEL

units.text: Mercy lets the rope go slack.
Ezra does not move.
The windlass creaks as the bucket swings.
We have a filed claim.
units.name: MERCY

units.text: You have a filed claim in the wrong county.
units.name: ANSEL

units.text: That so.
units.name: EZRA

units.text: I'm afraid it is.
units.name: ANSEL

units.text: He takes a folded paper from his coat and holds it out.
Ezra does not take it.
Ansel sets it on the windlass crank and steps back.
You have until sundown.
units.name: ANSEL

units.text: There's water down there.
units.name: MERCY

units.text: There's mud.
units.name: ANSEL

units.text: It's water, mister. Give us an hour.
units.name: MERCY

units.text: Ansel looks at the shaft, then at the horizon.
He sighs and removes his hat.
Sweat runs from his hair.
One hour. Then I'm obliged to read it aloud.
units.name: ANSEL

units.text: He walks to the shade of the wagon and sits on its tongue.
Ezra waits.
Then he climbs back down the ladder into the shaft.
Mercy takes up the rope again, steady as a post, and begins to haul.
